secoes.titulo: How to choose the first process
secoes.sub: From the list of candidates to the next course, in five steps. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: List three processes that run with people today and that already have, or soon will have, AI around them. Use the diagnosis from lesson 6: tools with no owner usually point to where the process is.

What stays is what has volume (it happens every week), a rule you can write down (someone can explain right from wrong), and known damage (you know what can go wrong and what it costs). These filters come from this course, to help you choose where to start.
The process you choose gets a business owner, with a name, who answers for the result from end to end. Without an owner, the process becomes just another disconnected project.
Two or three measures of the process as it is, taken before any change: how many cases, how many corrected, how much time. It is the starting point that was missing from the Hora dashboard.

Your biggest question about the process picks the course: should it exist this way? G2. How do I hand it to the agent? G3. Which model and how much does it cost? G4. What about the people? G1. How do I govern and measure? G5.

secoes.legenda: The recommendation to start with a process from your own company comes from the AI Management Area ("Start now"). The three filters are a tool from this course.

secoes.sub: Four steps. Horizonte (a fictional study company) does the practice run; your process is the one that counts.

texto: Whoever starts with the tool ends up looking for a process that fits it. Whoever starts with the process first asks whether it should still exist this way, and only then chooses a person, an agent or automation.
Pick just one. The first process is for learning to manage; the second comes out faster.

exemplo.texto: Candidates: the order that comes in by WhatsApp through to invoicing, collections (which Carlos wants to hand to Hora in November) and the daily customer service summary.

texto: Volume: it happens every week, in an amount worth looking at. Rule: someone can write down what is right and wrong. Damage: you know what can go wrong and how big the mess would be.
A process that fails the third filter is not forbidden; it just isn't the first one. Start where the error is known and can be contained.

exemplo.texto: The order passes all three: 141 to 171 orders per week on the dashboard, a written discount policy and known damage (discount, large order). Collections has no written rule yet.

texto: Choose two or three measures the process already lets you count: how many cases, how many needed correction, how much time from start to finish. Measure for two weeks, as it is, without changing anything.
Without this starting point, any number afterward becomes an impression. It is failure F11 from the lab: the dashboard started on the day Hora was turned on.

exemplo.texto: Measure for two weeks: orders accepted without correction at picking, hours from order to invoicing, and exceptions per day. Owner: Patrícia.

texto: Write your biggest question about the process in one sentence. It picks the course: G2 if it is "should it exist this way?", G3 if it is "how do I hand it to the agent and how far does it go?", G4 if it is model and cost, G1 if it is the people, G5 if it is governing and measuring.
The program's suggested order (G0, G2, G3, G4, G1, G5) applies when there is no urgency. A present risk beats the order.

exemplo.texto: Patrícia's biggest question is "how far can Hora go on its own?". Next course: G3. Then G2, to redesign the order.

abas.html:
Sales · Horizonte Distribuidora · fictional study company · numbers from the lab dashboard

  • Chosen: order that comes in by WhatsApp through to invoicing.
  • Owner: Patrícia Lima · systems: Rafael.
  • Volume: 141 to 171 orders closed per week and 702 to 901 Hora interactions per week (Sep–Oct/2026, dashboard).
  • AI present: Hora; the sales team's email assistant.
  • Today's measure (two weeks): % of orders accepted without correction at picking; hours from order to invoicing; exceptions per day.
  • Biggest question: how far can Hora go on its own? Next course: G3; then G2.
  • Rubric: 85/100, 4 of 4 required.

1. The process has a start and an end that anyone in the area recognizes.
  2. Each number has a source (dashboard, system, hand count).
  3. Today's measure has a period and an owner, and is taken before anything changes.
  4. Common mistake: choosing the flashiest process. The first one is the one with volume, rule and known damage.

exemplo.texto: Choose the process and the measure before the tool. If the tool changes, the process and the starting point still hold.

texto: Gartner (2026): only 17% of companies have agents in use, worldwide. GFT, Tech Trends 2026 LATAM with data from BCG: 18% of Brazilian companies integrate agents, versus 13% worldwide.
Different definitions, same reading: if you are just starting now, you are not behind most others.

exemplo.texto: One well-chosen, well-measured process is worth more than five agents switched on with no owner.

texto: Okta, AI Agents at Work 2026 (vendor survey): almost two thirds of organizations apply weaker controls to agents than to people. Deloitte (09/17/2026): 27% of Brazilian companies have mature governance.
Gartner (02/17/2026, forecast): spending on AI governance rises from US$ 492 million in 2026 to more than US$ 1 billion in 2030.

exemplo.texto: Owner, permissions and logging go into your first process from day one, not after the first scare.

texto: Microsoft, Work Trend Index 2026 (05/2026, vendor survey): when the manager uses AI in front of the team, perceived value goes up 17 points. IT Forum (2026, opinion column): the year companies stop building agents and start operating them.
Next review of this dashboard: January 2027. What is method (lessons 1 to 7) does not change; what is product and numbers does.

exemplo.texto: The person who leads the first process is the manager of the area, in front of the team. Don't outsource the example.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Where should the program start, according to this lesson?
opcoes: With the newest tool on the market
With a process in your company, chosen by volume, rules and known damage
perguntas.explica: Tools change in months; the process and the measure stay. The three filters help you pick a first process where you can learn without big damage.

perguntas.p: Why measure the process for two weeks before changing anything?
opcoes: To produce a report for the board
To have the starting point that lets you say, later, whether it got better
Because the agent needs data to train
perguntas.explica: Without a starting point, every number that comes later becomes an impression. That is what happened with Hora's dashboard, which started on the day it was turned on.

perguntas.p: Your biggest question is "should this checking step still exist?" Which course comes next?
perguntas.explica: Asking whether a step should exist is work architecture: the subject of G2, which teaches you to take the process apart before automating it.

perguntas.p: AgentKit's Agent Builder will be shut down on 11/30/2026. What does this teach about the first process?
opcoes: That it is better to wait for the tools to stabilize
That the process and the measure should be chosen before the tool, because they outlast the tool's replacement
That you should only use one vendor's brand
perguntas.explica: Products get discontinued and change price within months. If you chose the process and measured the baseline, you can switch tools without losing what you learned.
